deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a fair-copy page of German lecture or study notes on ancient history: the wars of the Diadochi after Alexander the Great. It continues from folio 148, which covers the winter campaign of Antigonus against Eumenes in Media, Persis and Susiana.

Content, paraphrased:
(1) Eumenes could not rely on his army. Antigonus seized the baggage of the Argyraspides (the 'Silver Shields'), who were so undisciplined that they had brought their families along. The families were captured too. This is the aftermath of the battle of Gabiene.
(2) The Argyraspides negotiated with Antigonus. His condition was that they hand over Eumenes. They did, and Eumenes was executed in front of the army; the notes date this to 315.
(3) A new heading follows: 'Dritter Zeitabschnitt. Vom Tode des Eumenes bis zum Tode des Antigonus, 315 – 301' (Third period: from the death of Eumenes to the death of Antigonus, 315–301).
(4) Antigonus had himself proclaimed King of Asia at Persepolis. Several satraps were deposed and others removed. He demanded that Seleucus render accounts. Seleucus refused and fled to Ptolemy; the sentence continues on the next folio.

There are no formulas, computations or mathematical problems. Nothing needs to be reconstructed mathematically.

The handwriting and content suggest school or university history notes, probably copied or attended by someone in Gauss's circle. They are not a mathematical working sheet. Whether the hand is Gauss's own is unsure; it does not look like his usual mathematical hand.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: the execution of Eumenes after Gabiene is now usually dated to winter 316/315 BC (often given as 316). The '315' here follows an older Diodorus-based chronology. This is acceptable for its time.

Historical nuance: Antigonus did not formally take the royal title until 306 BC. In 316/315 at Persepolis he acted as lord of Asia. Calling it a proclamation as 'König von Asien' is an imprecision common in older textbooks.
The end date 301 (death of Antigonus at Ipsus) is correct.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is non-mathematical history notes on the Diadochi wars, with no mathematical content. It is of archival interest only, as evidence of the non-mathematical material bound into this bundle.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the '†' in 'konnte sich † seine Armee' is likely the writer's abbreviation sign. The sense is 'konnte sich auf seine Armee nicht verlassen'.
Line 3: 'Bagage' is plausible. The word is partly overwritten, with a correction mark in a different (bluish) ink.
Line 5: 'Sie traten' may read 'Die traten'. The meaning is unaffected.
Heading: 'bis z[um] † des Antigonus' should be read as 'bis zum Tode des Antigonus'. The † symbol consistently stands for 'Tod' on this page.
Heading: 'Zeitabschnitt' has a vertical correction stroke between 'Zeit' and 'abschnitt' in blue ink.
Line 'andere wurden mit Gewalt weggeschafft': 'mit Gewalt' is uncertain; the image may read 'andere wurden mit ... weggeschafft'. 'weggeschafft' is the likely reading.
'ein{+e+} Rechnung ablegen' is correct: 'eine Rechnung ablegen' (render accounts).
